landmarks.name: Masjid al-Haram
landmarks.writeup: The largest mosque in the world, located in Mecca, it surrounds Islam's holiest site, the Kaaba.

wiki.extract: Masjid al-Haram, also known as the Great Mosque of Mecca, is a mosque in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, serving as the holiest and most important mosque in Islam. As of 2026, the Great Mosque is the largest mosque and most expensive building in the world.

landmarks.name: Al-Masjid an-Nabawi
landmarks.writeup: The Prophet's Mosque in Medina, second holiest site in Islam, known for its green dome.

wiki.extract: The king of Saudi Arabia, officially the king of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, is head of state of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, who holds absolute power. He is the head of the Saudi Arabian royal family, the House of Saud. The king is the commander-in-chief of the Saudi Arabian Armed Forces and the head of the Saudi national honors system. The king is called the "Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques", a title that signifies Saudi Arabia's jurisdiction over the mosques of Masjid al-Haram in Mecca and Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in Medina. The title has been used many times through the history of Islam. The first Saudi king to use the title was Faisal; however, King Khalid did not use the title after him. In 1986, King Fahd replaced "His Majesty" with the title of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, and it has been since used by both King Abdullah and King Salman. The king has been named the most powerful and influential Muslim and Arab leader in the world according to The Muslim 500.

landmarks.name: Diriyah
landmarks.writeup: Historic town near Riyadh, birthplace of the Saudi state and a UNESCO World Heritage site.

wiki.extract: Diriyah is a town and governorate in Saudi Arabia. Located on the northwestern outskirts of the Saudi capital, Riyadh, Diriyah was the original home of the House of Saud, and served as the capital of the Emirate of Diriyah under the first Saudi dynasty from 1727 to 1818. Today, the town is the seat of the Diriyah Governorate, which also includes the villages of Uyayna, Jubayla, and Al-Ammariyyah, among others—and is part of Riyadh Province.

landmarks.name: Edge of the World
landmarks.writeup: A dramatic cliff offering panoramic views over the surrounding desert landscape.

wiki.extract:
Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud is King of Saudi Arabia, having reigned since 2015. He is a son of King Abdulaziz, the founder of Saudi Arabia, and a member of the House of Saud.
Salman is the third-oldest living head of state and the oldest living monarch. He is the first Saudi head of state born after the unification of Saudi Arabia.

landmarks.name: Madain Saleh
landmarks.writeup: Archaeological site with well-preserved Nabatean tombs, Saudi Arabia's first UNESCO World Heritage site.

wiki.extract: Hegra, also known as Madāʾin Ṣāliḥ, is an archaeological site located in the area of Al-'Ula within Medina Province in the Hejaz region, Saudi Arabia.

head_of_state: King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud

cultural_events.name: Janadriyah Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Annual cultural festival celebrating Saudi heritage, including traditional music, dance, and crafts.

cultural_events.name: Riyadh Season
cultural_events.writeup: A months-long entertainment festival featuring concerts, sports, and cultural events.

cultural_events.name: Hajj
cultural_events.writeup: The annual Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca, one of the Five Pillars of Islam, attracting millions of Muslims worldwide.

food_writeup: Saudi cuisine features dishes like Kabsa, a spiced rice and meat dish, and dates, which are culturally significant. Meals often include lamb, chicken, rice, and a variety of spices reflecting Arabian Peninsula flavors.
brief_history: Saudi Arabia was unified in 1932 by King Abdulaziz Al Saud. It is the birthplace of Islam and home to its two holiest cities, Mecca and Medina. The discovery of oil in 1938 transformed its economy and global significance.

important_people.name: King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud

current_conflicts: Saudi Arabia is involved in the Yemen conflict, supporting the Yemeni government against Houthi rebels. It also faces regional tensions with Iran and ongoing concerns over terrorism and security.
